<objective>
Create the shared, form-agnostic logic layer that both `upload-modal` and `attachment-edit-modal` will consume (D-01, D-03): one coordinate-transform utility, one `MeasurementRulerService` (ruler drag lifecycle + pixel-length math), and one `AttachmentPointDefinitionService` (click-to-place coordinate math). This is a behavior-preserving relocation of logic that currently exists near-identically in both modals — no new abstractions, no new libraries (RESEARCH.md forbids `@angular/cdk`).

The hard design rule (D-01 consequence, RESEARCH.md Pitfall 1 & 5): these services emit plain value objects (`MeasurementLine`, `{x, y}`) via observables/return values and NEVER import `@angular/forms`, reach into a parent `FormGroup`, or emit a full `AttachmentPoint`. Each parent modal owns its own form writes and its own `AttachmentPoint` id/name construction.

Purpose: Eliminate the near-line-for-line duplication that codebase scouting flagged as the most concrete problem (per 01-CONTEXT.md Specific Ideas), and produce the reusable pieces Waves 3-4 wire into presentational components and thinned modal shells.
Output: Three new source files + three spec files under `src/app/utils/` and `src/app/services/`.
</objective>

<task type="auto" tdd="true">
  <name>Task 1: Extract the display→original coordinate transform into a shared util</name>
  <files>src/app/utils/coordinate-transform.ts, src/app/utils/coordinate-transform.spec.ts</files>
  <read_first>
    - src/app/components/upload-modal/upload-modal.component.ts lines 633-668 (onImageClick transform + bounds reject) and lines 829-875 (onRulerPointMove transform + clamp), 944-962 (getScaledRulerX/Y display scaling)
    - src/app/utils/measurement-utils.ts and src/app/utils/measurement-utils.spec.ts (existing pure-util + spec convention to mirror for file shape, imports grouping, kebab-case)
    - src/app/models/image-model.interface.ts (MeasurementLine + AttachmentPoint shapes)
  </read_first>
  <behavior>
    - `toOriginalCoords(clientX, clientY, imageEl)` returns `{ x, y, inDisplayBounds }` where x/y = `Math.round((clientX - rect.left) * (naturalWidth / width))` and the y-analog, exactly matching upload-modal lines 649-650 & 851-852; `inDisplayBounds` is true when the display-space offset is within `[0, rect.width] × [0, rect.height]` (mirrors the reject condition at upload-modal lines 644-646).
    - `clampToNatural(x, y, imageEl)` returns coordinates clamped to `[0, naturalWidth] × [0, naturalHeight]` (mirrors `Math.max(0, Math.min(...))` at upload-modal lines 857-859).
    - `displayFromOriginal(originalX, originalY, imageEl)` returns display-space px = `originalX * (width / naturalWidth)` and analog (mirrors getScaledRulerX/Y at lines 944-962) so ruler-marker SVG positioning has one source too.
    - Given naturalWidth=800/width=400 and a click at client offset 100px from rect.left → original x = 200.
  </behavior>
  <action>
    Create `src/app/utils/coordinate-transform.ts` exporting the three pure functions above. Each takes an `HTMLImageElement` (reads `getBoundingClientRect()`, `naturalWidth`/`naturalHeight`, `width`/`height`) and returns plain numbers/objects — no DOM mutation, no `@angular/forms` import, no service dependency. Preserve the existing `Math.round` and clamp behavior byte-for-byte so numeric output is identical to the inlined formulas in both modals. Do NOT introduce a bounds policy inside the util: return `inDisplayBounds` as data and let each caller decide (ruler clamps; point-placement rejects) — this keeps both existing behaviors intact. Create `coordinate-transform.spec.ts` covering the naturalWidth/width scaling, the round-to-integer behavior, the clamp min/max at both edges, and the in/out-of-display-bounds flag, following the assertion style in `measurement-utils.spec.ts`.
  </action>
  <verify>
    <automated>pnpm exec ng test --include='**/coordinate-transform.spec.ts' --watch=false --browsers=ChromeHeadless</automated>
  </verify>
  <acceptance_criteria>
    - `coordinate-transform.spec.ts` passes with cases for scaling ratio, rounding, both clamp edges, and the in/out-of-bounds flag.
    - `grep -E "^import" src/app/utils/coordinate-transform.ts | grep -c "@angular/forms"` returns 0 (no forms coupling).
    - The scaling formula in the util matches `naturalWidth / width` / `naturalHeight / height` (same as upload-modal lines 649-650, 851-852).
  </acceptance_criteria>
  <done>One shared, tested coordinate-transform util exists; ruler and point-placement callers can both use it instead of inlining the formula.</done>
</task>

<threat_model>
## Trust Boundaries

| Boundary | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| pointer/touch event → coordinate math | User-controlled `MouseEvent`/`TouchEvent` clientX/clientY cross into pixel-coordinate computation that produces persisted attachment points and measurement lines. |

## STRIDE Threat Register

| Threat ID | Category | Component | Severity | Disposition | Mitigation Plan |
|-----------|----------|-----------|----------|-------------|-----------------|
| T-01-01 | Tampering | coordinate-transform util, MeasurementRulerService move handler, AttachmentPointDefinitionService | low | mitigate | Preserve the existing bounds handling verbatim: ruler CLAMPS to `[0,natural]` (upload lines 857-859), point-placement REJECTS out-of-display-bounds and returns null (upload lines 644-646). Do not simplify or drop either during relocation. |
| T-01-03 | Denial of Service | MeasurementRulerService document listeners | low | mitigate | Provide `stopDragDefensively()` removing all four listener types; contract requires every consumer's `ngOnDestroy` to call it (enforced in Wave 3/4 plans). |
| T-01-SC | Tampering | npm/pnpm installs | high | accept | No packages installed this plan; `@angular/cdk`/DnD libs explicitly forbidden by RESEARCH.md. |
</threat_model>
